findings: Raw artifact hashes, named content-map hashes and context-bearing binding hashes are different identity roles; their distinct counts are not missing-file or execution counts.
Package bindings include workspace and installed-package paths. Dependency identities can include generated configuration, private transient fixture inputs and tool snapshots.
The prepared-result publication uses raw file bytes, while package bindings, qualification environments and runtime maps use their own canonical-object conventions.
Ten retained original macOS full bindings and two environment/runtime objects match the recorded identities. The prepared-result raw file matches references in all sixteen macOS receipts.
The new fixed raw-file metadata lookup returned the already-known macOS publication only. Seven identities were unlocated in that prefix, not proven globally absent.
Original metadata identity does not establish retained dependency trees, historical custody, available executable environments or whole semantic reference completeness.
limits: This is a minimized reporting derivative. Public checks do not open original metadata, reproduce the private lookup or execute products.
